idiom_name: module-level ContextVar with set()/get()/reset() (and Token as context manager)
implementation_notes: contextvars is the stdlib's ambient slot: a Value set with var.set(value) is visible to every function called below it in the same context, and asyncio gives each Task a copy of the current context, so request data set at the top of a task reaches all of its awaits without being threaded through signatures. copy_context() plus Context.run() enter a scope explicitly (and Context implement Mapping for inspection), while the Token returned by set() restores the previous value. Declare ContextVars at module level: Context objects hold strong references, so variables created in closures are not garbage collected.
code_sketch:
from contextvars import ContextVar

current_user: ContextVar[User | None] = ContextVar('current_user', default=None)

async def handler(request):
    token = current_user.set(await authenticate(request))
    try:
        await render()            # current_user.get() works at any depth
    finally:
        current_user.reset(token)
pitfalls: A ContextVar set inside a child task does not affect the parent: each Task runs in a copy of the context, which surprises code that expects writes to propagate back.
Relying on the default value when the value is genuinely required hides a missing provider - raise instead of returning a plausible default.
Creating ContextVars inside closures or per-call keeps them alive through the enclosing Context, leaking memory; declare them at module level.

variants.name: Flask application/request context proxies (current_app, g)
variants.idiom_name: current_app / g / LocalProxy context locals pushed per request
variants.implementation_notes: Web frameworks package the same idea as an explicitly pushed context: Flask pushes an application context (and a request context) when a request starts, pops them when it ends, and exposes the data as proxies - current_app for the application, g as a per-context namespace - so no function needs the app passed in and LocalProxy(get_db) turns any context-scoped factory into such a proxy. Reading a proxy without a pushed context fails immediately (RuntimeError: Working outside of application context) rather than returning a stale default, which is the fail-loud variant of the missing-provider case.
pitfalls: g lives exactly as long as the context: storing its values in a background task or a module-level cache keeps objects alive after teardown - copy what you need during the request.
A worker thread or a fresh asyncio Task started inside the request does not inherit the pushed context, so proxies raise the outside-context error there; pass the values explicitly instead.
Proxies are untyped at runtime: a missing key on g surfaces as an AttributeError deep in the call stack rather than at the point where the app pushed the context.
